sources_opened.pages: Held source for DurrettPTEAuthor2019 (held-sources.json entry, Version 5, 490 PDF pages; hash verified). Cited locators pp. 210, 214--216 read in full: PDF 218 = printed p. 210 (Example 4.1.8 Borel's paradox; Theorem 4.1.9 and remark); PDF 222 = p. 214 (Section 4.1.3 r.c.d. definition with (ii) for a.e. omega, r.c.p. special case, continuation of Example 4.1.6 with f>0, Theorem 4.1.16 and proof, Dieudonne non-existence remark); PDF 223 = p. 215 (Theorems 4.1.17 and 4.1.18 with proofs); PDF 224 = p. 216 (Exercises 4.1.1--4.1.8, including 4.1.4 conditional Hoelder). Also consulted outside the cited extent: PDF 213--214 = pp. 205--206 (conditional expectation defined for E|X|<infinity) and PDF 61 = p. 53 (definition of a nice space).

defect_observations.observation: Stale queue/packet records. The body file now hashes b337636c... (queue destination and packet w02b-p15-008 record 02f6e868... and 254 lines; it now has 257). Lines 45-47 (cross-reference to sec:p15-w02b-p15-008-ae-kernels) were inserted into def:p15-regular-conditional-law, so C002's exact_current_text is no longer verbatim and the queue body_lines for C002-C012 are off by +3 (C002 is now 31-53, C012 is 250-257). The packet's driver records (parts/p15.tex 85 lines, annex/p15.tex 83 lines) are also stale. No coverage consequence; the annex hash still matches the queue.

The uniqueness step asserts that the pulled-back rational half-lines generate S without giving the reason (phi is a measurable isomorphism and thm:p15-measurability-criterion's generated-sigma-algebra clause). This is a one-line inference that is not cited.

The value-conditional-law proof reuses the real-law and transport arguments by reference ('apply to H_q(Y)', 'the same Borel-image and transport arguments as above'). The referenced arguments are written in full at annex 47-181 and apply verbatim, so this was accepted. A stricter house rule against 'same as above' would need these few lines expanded.

The cross-product length cos(phi) and the trigonometric identities giving r(Theta',Psi) = r(Theta,Phi) are asserted, not displayed. They support explanatory or definitional remarks in def:p15-sphere-coordinate-law, not the stated theorem conclusions. 'Normalized spherical area law' relies on the usual parametrized area element, which is not developed in P15.

'That special case needs an existence hypothesis on the outcome space itself' is supported only by the source's Dieudonne citation, which is repeated at w02b-p15-008 body 235-239. No non-existence example is supplied. The definition does not owe one, and the sentence also reads as a scope remark matching the C012 boundary.
